# Retained world, scene and prefab files

Saves written by `World::save` at a recorded engine revision, kept so that
later revisions are tested against bytes they did not write themselves.
[STABILITY.md](../../../STABILITY.md#saved-worlds) promises that saves from
earlier releases keep loading; `tests/save_compat.rs` checks that promise
against the world file, and `tests/prefab_compat.rs` loads the world file as a
scene (a scene is the saved-world format) and spawns the prefab through the
game-facing loaders, `Ctx::load_scene` and `Ctx::spawn_prefab`.

| Fixture | Format | Save version | Engine revision | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `world_v1.json` | `crabby-world` | 1 | `51323ef` (ponko 0.0.1) | `world_v1.provenance.json` |
| `prefab_v1.json` | `crabby-prefab` | 1 | `b3799f6` (ponko 0.0.1) | `prefab_v1.provenance.json` |

`world_v1.json` is a baseline taken from the engine's `main` branch, not from
a published release: it shows that the current loader reads what that revision
wrote, not that any earlier binary release is covered.

## What a fixture covers

- The save header (`format`, `version`) and the `entities`, `resources` and
  `not_saved` sections.
- Entity ids with gaps and generations, and components that refer to other
  entities (`Attached`, a game component holding an `Entity`).
- The saved fields of built-in components (`Transform2D`, `Attached`).
- Game components written with serde: structs, tuple structs, enums, options,
  strings with escapes and non-ASCII text.
- Reflected resources.

The test asserts the decoded world field by field, so adding a field with a
default to a built-in component does not fail it; removing or renaming one does.

## Rules

- **Never edit or regenerate a retained fixture** to make a test pass. A
  failing test means old saves no longer load: fix the loader, add a
  migration, or make an explicit compatibility decision (see STABILITY.md).
- Fixtures are generated by the `#[ignore]`d `write_v*_fixture` function in
  `tests/save_compat.rs`, never by hand and never inside a regression test.
  The generator refuses to overwrite an existing file.

## Adding a fixture for a new save version

1. Copy `write_v1_fixture` to `write_v<N>_fixture` (keep the old one), and
   make it build a world that uses what the new version adds.
2. Generate it from a clean checkout of the revision that introduces the version:

   ```sh
   PONKO_SAVE_FIXTURE_OUT=$PWD/tests/fixtures/saves/world_v<N>.json \
     cargo test -p ponko --no-default-features --test save_compat -- --ignored --exact write_v<N>_fixture
   ```

3. Write `world_v<N>.provenance.json` with the same keys as the v1 file: the
   full commit id (`git rev-parse HEAD`), `rustc --version`, the command and
   the date.
4. Add loader tests for it that assert the decoded state, and keep the tests
   for every older fixture.

## Prefab fixtures

`prefab_v1.json` is written by `Assets::save_prefab`. Its generator is the
`#[ignore]`d `write_prefab_v1_fixture` in `tests/prefab_compat.rs`, with the
same rules as above (never edited by hand, never regenerated, refuses to
overwrite):

```sh
PONKO_PREFAB_FIXTURE_OUT=$PWD/tests/fixtures/saves/prefab_v<N>.json \
  cargo test -p ponko --no-default-features --test prefab_compat -- --ignored --exact write_prefab_v<N>_fixture
```

The tests check that the position is the spawner's while rotation, scale and
every other component come from the file, and that unsupported versions, other
formats and empty prefabs fail with a message and spawn nothing.
